files.role: Physical run-length encoding: raw/adaptive run widths, mini chunk construction and child candidates, framed whole blocks, strict and legacy-clamping eager readers, validated unexpanded u16 runs and38 test functions.
files.limits: All3414 source lines read in bounded untruncated outputs in ANALYZE78. No repository build/test/lint/benchmark/generator/install or network. Edge cases and performance costs are source deductions, not runtime reproduction. Partial primitive caller remains pending.
ranges: SPDX and module docs introduce two RLE buffers: one value per physical run and its unsigned8/16/32 repeat count. Values are not globally unique: nonadjacent equal values or width/chunk splits repeat entries. Example i32[1,1,1,2,2,3,3,3,3] becomes values[1,2,3], lengths[3,2,4]. U8 splits runs at255; wider lengths reduce splitting.

Docs list8/16/32/64 integer/float widths and claim automatic run count<50% plus2048-value mini cap. Those statements are stale: shared policy applies a fraction only if explicit and compares byte costs; current lazy cap defaults4096 and clamps environment override1..32768. Block frame is one u64LE value-buffer byte size followed by value bytes then length bytes. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:174-267; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-34)

Imports connect ArrowNativeType/ScalarBuffer, trace logging, LanceBuffer/DataBlock, shared compression traits/payload guard, mini constants and metadata, general child compressor factory, protobuf helper and Lance errors. No production async, IO or local unsafe block; typed borrowing may share or copy depending alignment. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:145-172)

Crate-internal Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq RunLengthWidth variants U8/U16/U32 represent literal repeat counts, maxima255/65535/4294967295. from_bits accepts8/16/32 elseNone; bits_per_value returns width; private bytes_per_value/max_run_length map to1/2/4 and native unsigned maxima. No zero-based length offset.

Private write_length narrows to selected unsigned type without bounds check and writes LE; read_length indexes exactly1/2/4 bytes without checking available length. Callers must validate. Private RUN_LENGTH_WIDTHS order[U8,U16,U32] defines cost-tie preference.

Crate-internal select_run_length_width_from_entries requires exactly3 entry counts and value width8/16/32/64, otherwise contextual InvalidInputSource. Starts U8, compares payload costs using strict less, retaining narrower width on equal cost. Does not validate whether entry counts are realizable/ordered or include headers/child compression.

Crate-internal rle_encoded_size_from_entries multiplies u128 entry count by floor(valuebits/8)+lengthbytes without its own width validation. run_length_width_index maps widths to0/1/2. select_run_length_width and rle_encoded_size first collect counts from actual data/count/width/optional segmentation then select or index cost. These are scans/estimates, not encoded output.

Private collection checked-converts count to usize, macro checked-multiplies by native value bytes, requires exact physical data length, borrows unsigned typed words and bounds-checks prefix. Width dispatch8/16/32/64 elseInvalidInput. Empty exact buffer returns all-zero counts through slice helper. Signed/floating values compare raw unsigned bit patterns. Typed borrowing can copy unaligned bytes; no statistic cache.

Generic run scan returns[0;3] for empty; otherwise compares adjacent values, accumulates each maximal run and final run. current_length increment is ordinary u64 addition. Equality is raw unsigned for actual dispatch; the generic helper itself uses T PartialEq. No null bitmap or logical schema enters.

Crate-internal accumulate_run_length_entries uses supplied segment cap or run_length, clamped to at least1, splits each run independently, and saturating-adds ceil(segment/width_max) to three counters. Zero run contributes nothing. This estimator segments each run, not a global chunk cursor, and ignores MAX_MINIBLOCK_BYTES/power-of-two boundaries, so it need not equal actual mini payload size.

Public Debug RleEncoder stores private width, optional values/run-length general configs and child-bitpacking bool. Private Clone RleChildCandidate stores descriptor, LanceBuffer, per-chunk u32 sizes, aggregate usize size and external-count dependency. Encoder Default delegates public new. No shared mutable state or codec cache in encoder itself.

Public new selects U8, no general children and no bitpacking. Crate-internal with_run_length_width changes width only; with_child_encoding accepts independent child configs and bitpacking flag unchecked. Their names are constructors, not consuming builders. Whole-block compression later ignores child configs/flag.

Private encode_data handles declared0 immediately with empty buffer/chunk vectors, before checking input bytes or width. Otherwise checked usize count; estimate runs=count/10, reserve value/length capacities with unchecked products, then prepare global append buffers and offset/remaining cursor. Initial10:1 ratio is allocation guess, not threshold.

Each mini iteration dispatches unsigned native chunk encoder, unsupported width InvalidInput. Zero progress yields Internal with remaining count, offset, physical length, width and cap, discarding partial local output through Result. Unlike block encoder no up-front exact byte-length check. Subsequent typed borrow can panic for non-divisible clipped buffers.

Last chunk stores log_num_values0; nonlast asserts processed count power-of-two then stores ilog2 as u8. Append MiniBlockChunk with per-child new byte lengths cast to u32, update cursor/remaining and loop. Return exactly two global buffers for nonempty input. Global vectors own all chunks; consumers must slice using buffer_sizes rather than treat them as independently framed chunks.

Whole-block dispatch validates width even for count0. Generic path checked-converts count, checked-multiplies byte size and requires exact input length. Empty valid input returns two present empty buffers. Nonempty borrows complete unsigned slice, reserves count/10 estimates then encodes all runs without mini count/byte splitting. Surplus input is rejected here, unlike mini encoding which only visits declared values.

Rolling mini chunk bounds prefix by remaining count and lazy max values. Byte offset/end products are unchecked; clips end to data length, returns zero progress if start beyond data or typed slice empty. Computes encoded size for full available prefix. If all declared remaining values fit cap and payload<=8186, mark final; else choose largest valid power-of-two prefix. Then encode exactly that prefix, returning physical run count and consumed values. Clipped short input eventually errors when remaining values cannot progress. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-34)

largest_power_of_two_prefix starts highest power<=min(actual typed length,cap) using ilog2, repeatedly halves until a prefix>1 fits payload budget, elseNone. Standalone empty input would panic at ilog2, but local caller returns early for empty typed data. One-value nonfinal chunks are forbidden because log0 is final sentinel; configured cap1 can make nontrivial input fail progress.

encoded_size scans adjacent runs and sums run_size for each, using usize arithmetic. run_size=ceil(length/selected_max)*(sizeofT+lengthbytes). Zero slice costs0. Repeated prefix-size scans add CPU before final encode; no headers/structural levels/padding/child codec sizes included.

encode_values scans maximal adjacent-equal runs and calls add_run. add_run borrows native value bytes with bytemuck, reserves full+remainder entries, emits repeated value plus max length for every full-width segment, then remainder ifpositive. Exact multiples emit no zero remainder. Values use host representation under crate little-endian gate; lengths explicitly LE. Returned combined bytes are unchecked usize products/sum. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:27-31)

flat_child_candidate creates Flat(bits,None), clones selected global LanceBuffer and collects matching per-chunk sizes; size is buffer len and count dependency false. Indexing assumes two valid buffers and corresponding chunk sizes; does not validate coverage or alignment. Buffer clone shares underlying Arrow allocation.

General child candidate skips absent/empty selected buffer, constructs requested compressor or propagates error, then compresses each original chunk into one concatenated Vec. Checked offset addition/bounds and u32 compressed chunk size; total original size addition unchecked. Candidate only if aggregate compressed bytes strictly less than visited original bytes; individual chunks may expand. Retains selected config in General(Flat) descriptor and marks count-independent. No final offset==original len check, but normal encode_data sizes cover it. Codec/metadata failure propagates instead of ignoring optional candidate.

Feature-gated bitpacked child rejects empty buffer, computes one required bit width across all runs and refuses width>=native. Creates OutOfLineBitpacking using this global compressed width, then prepares packed bytes/per-chunk sizes and checked conversion of nativebytewidth. Bit width minimum is1 even when every value is0.

Per bitpacked child chunk checked-adds/bounds offset, rejects zero nativebytes or nonmultiple chunk size, derives physical run count from bytes, builds fixed block and calls OutOfLine blockcompressor. Missing payload Internal; oversized chunk u32 conversion InvalidInput. Appends payload and offsets; aggregate candidate must be strictly smaller than entire original buffer. Descriptor OutOfLine(native,Flat(packed,None)); requires external run count. No final coverage check local.

Feature-gated required_bits reads unsigned LE8/16/32/64 words, uses max value or0, returns max(bitlength,1). as_chunks remainder is ignored here; per-chunk validity later catches normal malformed sizes. Unsupported valuebits InvalidInput. No signed-magnitude or float numerical interpretation.

child_candidates always starts Flat, then optional General, then optional feature-enabled bitpacking. Without feature the flag is explicitly unused. No General-over-bitpacking candidate is written here although reader grammar accepts it. Candidate errors abort whole selection; configuration presence does not force General to win.

select_child_candidates enumerates value candidates outer and length candidates inner, excludes pairs where both need externalcount, minimizes unchecked usize sum strictly, so ties keep first ordering. Expects at least one viable pair (Flat invariant), then clones selected candidates; Arc-backed payload clones are cheap but per-chunk size Vec/descriptor clones can allocate. Other candidates live until function return.

Crate-internal selected_payload_size fully executes encode_data and both candidate generation paths, selects pair, returns saturating u128 combined size; empty returns0. It is not allocation-free estimation and excludes framing/padding/descriptors. Private with_size_from_data sets candidate size from actual owned buffer. Shared policy can invoke this then encode again. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:235-267)

MiniBlockCompressor impl ignores MiniBlockCompressionContext entirely and requires direct FixedWidth. encode_data empty shortcut returns empty data/chunks plus raw RLE(Flat originalbits,Flat lengthbits) descriptor, even if zero-count input has unsupported width or surplusbytes. No requested child config is used in empty path.

Nonempty mini compression generates both candidate lists, selects globally compatible pair, substitutes candidate sizes into each chunk while retaining logs, returns two selected global buffers/originalcount and RLE childdescriptors. No second per-chunk byte-budget test after childcompression; aggregate savings can coexist with expansion of one chunk. Wrong DataBlock kind InvalidInputSource.

BlockCompressor requires FixedWidth, calls strict raw whole-block encoder, stores values_size as u64LE in fresh Vec followed by all raw values and lengths; returns Some even for empty (8zero bytes). Descriptor children always Flat using selected widths. It does not use values_compression/run_lengths_compression/use_child_bitpacking. Other DataBlock kinds InvalidInput. CombinedVec grows without a precomputed capacity.

Public Debug RleDecompressor stores private value width, run width and two RleChildDecompressors. The crate-internal child stores its width and a private Flat or Block enum. Block contains a boxed decoder and a requires_num_values flag. There is no version parameter or mutable cache.

Crate-internal child constructors store unchecked widths and decoder/count dependencies. bits_per_value returns the stored width. Flat never requires a count; Block uses its flag. is_identity recognizes only the Flat enum arm.

Private child decode returns Flat bytes unchanged, without validating width or count. A count-dependent Block requires Some count; other Block children receive the optional count or zero. Decoder errors propagate, then extract_fixed_width validates the result. Zero serves as an unknown-count sentinel.

extract_fixed_width requires FixedWidth and the configured bit width. It checks block.num_values only when expected count is nonzero. It returns payload bytes without checking their length against the returned count. Errors include the child role and actual/expected values. Outer RLE checks paired physical sizes. General-wrapped Flat can deliberately return nonempty bytes with count zero. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:601-619)

Public new(valuebits) selects U8 lengths and raw children. Crate-internal constructors accept another run width or supplied children. Constructors do not validate widths or count dependencies; the shared factory normally does. Direct new can therefore retain an unsupported value width. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1238-1289)

decode_data returns empty FixedWidth immediately for declared count zero, ignoring buffer count/content, configured width and child dependencies. Positive count requires exactly two buffers, then decodes children and expands runs. The strict unexpanded reader differs. The block entry point still parses its outer frame before this shortcut.

decode_child_data dispatches eager expansion to unsigned u8/u16/u32/u64. Unsupported width returns InvalidInput. It wraps the expanded bytes with the configured width, external logical count and fresh BlockInfo. Original logical type and validity bitmap are not reconstructed here.

sum_run_lengths validates native value width and paired buffer divisibility/count, then folds little-endian literal lengths. It rejects zero entries and checked-adds into u64. It neither reads value contents nor expands values. Empty valid children sum to zero. This supports the narrow legacy inference hook.

validate_buffer_sizes requires values divisible by sizeof(T), lengths divisible by the selected length width, and equal numbers of physical entries. Errors describe both sizes/widths or both entry counts. It returns length bytes per entry without checking positivity, sum or expected logical count.

decode_child_buffers rejects two count-dependent children. If values need a count, it decodes lengths first and derives run count from their byte length; the reverse applies when lengths need a count. If neither needs a count, values then lengths receive None. Error precedence follows this order. It does not call infer_num_values.

num_child_values computes floor(bits/8), checked-converts to usize, rejects zero or a nondivisible buffer, and returns the quotient as u64. It does not independently require byte-aligned bits or a supported native width. Normal factory and outer checks establish those conditions. An empty child can yield the zero count sentinel.

Generic eager expansion accepts an empty child only with expected count zero; positive count with either empty child errors. Nonempty input validates paired sizes, borrows typed values, checked-converts logical count to usize and try_reserve_exact allocates the expanded vector. Allocation failure becomes InvalidInput. Historical mini runs may cross checkpoints, so mini decoding clamps overflow while block decoding rejects it. No version tag gates this behavior.

Every physical run rejects zero and checked-converts length. Strict overflow returns InvalidInput. Clamping overflow fills the remaining logical values and stops, ignoring subsequent entries. Final underflow errors. If exact coverage was already reached, a following zero still errors; a following positive entry triggers a zero-length clamp and stops. Trace logs count/type; initialized values are reinterpreted without unsafe set_len.

Mini decoding uses clamp=true; decoded_size checked-multiplies count by bits and divides upward by eight without width validation. Block decoding requires a payload, parses the frame and uses clamp=false. The inherited requires_payload is true. infer_num_values accepts only raw identity value16/lengthU8; other configurations return None before frame validation. The accepted signature sums raw lengths without expansion. A comment attributes this to Pylance 6.0.1 compatibility.

Private frame parsing requires at least eight bytes, reads u64 little-endian values_size, checked-converts it to usize, checked-adds the header and checks the result against total bytes. Returned slices are the value section and all remaining length bytes. Alignment, count, width and sums are checked elsewhere. Overflow wording depends on whether conversion or addition fails.

Private Clone/Debug RleRunLengths holds ScalarBuffer<u8/u16/u32>. try_new checks byte divisibility and borrows the corresponding type. Unaligned storage may be copied; aligned storage can be shared. Empty input is allowed. This constructor does not validate positive lengths or logical coverage.

Length access dispatches typed arrays; get directly indexes and casts to usize. owned_size counts visible scalar bytes. into_owned copies visible lengths to fresh storage. deep_size measures underlying buffer capacity. These measurements do not deduplicate shared allocations.

Crate-internal Clone/Debug RleRuns retains u16 values, original-width lengths, logical usize count and coalesced run count. Private try_new checked-converts count, checks u16 byte divisibility, parses lengths, requires equal physical counts and rejects empty runs for nonzero expected count. It preserves physical entries without expansion or merging.

RleRuns scans every entry, rejects zero, checked-adds coverage in usize and immediately rejects coverage beyond expected count. It counts adjacent value transitions, then requires exact final coverage. Declared zero does not bypass validation. Coalesced count groups adjacent equal values conceptually without changing buffers.

Crate-internal accessors return logical count, physical count, coalesced count and visible payload size. into_owned copies both visible arrays while retaining counts. deep_size sums backing capacities without Arc deduplication. Value/length access indexes directly and can panic out of bounds. iter is ExactSizeIterator over physical entries.

decode_u16_runs rejects non-16-bit values before parsing the frame, decoding children and strictly validating RleRuns. It accepts all run widths/children allowed by the supplied decoder. Primitive structural levels subsequently choose physical, coalesced or dense retention. That caller file is only partially reviewed and remains pending. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:1302-1380; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:1796-1800)

The private cfg(test) module imports shared strategies, Int32Array, rstest and general compression configuration. compress_miniblock supplies context(0,true,true). expand_u16_runs reserves logical count and repeats each physical run. These helpers do not perform IO or assert timing.

The lazy/eager u16 test uses 1000 ones, 500 zeros and 300 twos. Raw U8 lengths split 1800 values into eight physical runs. Assertions check exact eager bytes, logical count, eight physical runs, three coalesced runs and complete lazy expansion. Ownership/capacity behavior is not tested.

The empty lazy test accepts an eight-byte zero header and expected count zero, with all run counts zero. A zero-byte frame errors even for count zero. This tests frame validity before empty handling, unlike the mini shortcut.

Legacy inference constructs raw value16/lengthU8 data for 65543 logical values and asserts Some(count). A newer U32-length fixture with u32::MAX yields None from inference and strict overflow for expected 65535. Tests do not measure allocation or cover every rejected inference signature.

Four named rstest cases use value7 and one U8 length: zero/expected1, one/expected2, two/expected1, one/expected0. They assert InvalidInput and messages for zero, underflow and overflow, including strict validation of expected zero.

The general-feature lazy test encodes 4096 u16 values as 1024 runs of four, cycling 0..7. It manually compresses only the values child and rewrites the frame header, then constructs General(Flat16)+Flat8 through the shared factory. Strict lazy decoding and complete expansion must match. This tests reader composition rather than child compression by the block writer.

A constant 5000-value input has ceil(5000/255) physical runs and one coalesced run. A separate 200-value alternating input has 200 coalesced runs. Both assert exact expansion. A section comment introduces core tests.

The basic nine-i32 mini test checks logical count, one chunk and child sizes 12/3 bytes, without exact contents. Runs of 1000 times42 and 300 times100 require six U8 length entries. These assertions assume the default cap is sufficiently large.

The U16 mini test checks one i32 value entry, two length bytes equal to 1000 in little-endian order, and a Flat16 length descriptor. Direct decoding of the global buffers must produce all 1000 expected i32 values. U32 mini and selected chunks are not exercised here.

Two general-feature tests compress either values or lengths for 1024 runs of four cycling 0..7. They assert the General/Flat descriptor arrangement and exact full output through the default mini reader. Global buffers are decoded without slicing; the default 4096 cap permits one chunk. A smaller environment cap can change these fixture assumptions.

A bitpacking-gated reader test manually packs U8 lengths with OutOfLine(3,8), retains Flat32 values and builds the RLE descriptor. The default mini reader must reproduce all 4096 i32 values. Encoder candidate selection is not under test.

A bitpacking-gated descriptor with two count-dependent children must fail factory construction. test_general_compression is a private helper, not a test; it prefers compiled zstd level3, otherwise LZ4 without a level. repeating_runs cycles 0..7, expect_rle unwraps the RLE arm, and assert_decoded_i32_eq checks FixedWidth plus full typed equality.

A general-feature fixture of 8192 runs of four enables both child configurations. It asserts multiple chunks and General on both children, then slices/decompresses every chunk and checks complete values. Both children are count-independent, so this pair is permitted.

Two bitpacking-gated fixtures of 2048 runs of four test pair selection. Monotonic values select packed values/raw lengths; deterministic high-entropy values select raw values/packed lengths. Both decode sliced chunks and assert complete values. Exact payload cost is not asserted.

decompress_i32_chunks builds the default reader, tracks two buffer offsets and processed values, derives chunk counts from metadata, slices children and appends decoded i32 values. It asserts total logical count but not final consumption of both buffers. This is a test helper.

Bitpacking fixtures use monotonic run IDs or an LCG seeded7 with wrapping multiplier6364136223846793005 and increment1442695040888963407; the upper32 bits become i32. A width-choice test accumulates run300 with the configured cap and expects U16 at value width32; caps below300 can change that assumption. No tie or invalid-entry-count test appears here.

The all-types test invokes a generic helper for u8, u16, i32 including negatives, and u64. The helper copies native bytes, compresses/decompresses raw U8 RLE and checks only decoded byte length. Despite its name and PartialEq bound, it does not assert value equality. No float bit-pattern test is included.

Power-of-two tests use 1000/2500/5000/10000 i32 values in runs of50. Every nonfinal log must be positive and represent a power-of-two count within the cap; final log must be zero. They do not check total counts, exact chunk counts, byte budget or roundtrip.

Three rstest width cases U8/U16/U32 encode 4098 u16 values repeating1,0,0. Every chunk checks length alignment, paired entry count, summed run lengths versus declared chunk count, and total byte/logical consumption. The comment mentions a 2048 boundary, but the actual cap and byte budget determine splits.

Encoding empty bytes with declared one u16 must return Internal with remaining-count context. A positive-count decoder given one buffer must report the two-buffer requirement. One i32 value with two lengths must report inconsistent entries. The latter tests assert error text rather than the variant.

The U16 length-alignment test supplies one i32 value and a one-byte length buffer. It asserts InvalidInput and the divisibility-by-two message. No corresponding U32 remainder or native-value misalignment case appears here.

For one i32 value and U16 lengths, run4/expected5 errors on underflow, run6/expected5 clamps to exactly five ones in mini decoding, and run0 errors. A whole-block frame containing the same overflowing run must return InvalidInput. This establishes interface-dependent overflow behavior without a version gate.

The synthetic legacy checkpoint regression has i32 values7/8, U16 lengths2000/80 and expected2048. Mini decoding returns 2000 sevens and48 eights, ignoring the remaining32 repeats. It is a constructed regression input rather than a checked-in historical dataset.

Empty mini encoding emits no buffers; decoding no buffers at count zero returns empty FixedWidth. Tests do not combine zero count with surplus input, unsupported width or invalid child descriptors, nor test the empty block writer frame.

A 5000-i32 fixture contains 2000 times999, the sequence0..999 and2000 times777. It asserts two global buffers, manually slices chunks using sizes/logs, decodes each and checks full values. The Integration heading does not imply file IO or the production writer.

Seven explicit 1024-value patterns cover paired runs, constant42, alternating values, four runs of255 plus4, unique values, and two variants with a repeated final value. Fixtures are deterministic. Every input must have length1024.

Each boundary fixture compresses raw mini data and supplies whole global buffers to the reader, asserting1024 values,4096 bytes and exact contents. The error path distinguishes a4092-byte diagnostic. Default cap/budget permits one chunk for these fixtures; an environment override can change chunking.

The large low-repetition regression allocates1048576 i32 values and copied little-endian bytes. Starting at12345, an LCG with multiplier1664525 and increment1013904223 increments the value when bit16 is set. It compresses raw mini data and starts a diagnostic loop over five chunks. The nominal50% repeat rate is a deterministic criterion, not a selection-policy threshold.

The diagnostic loop computes unused chunk counts and prints nothing. The reader receives concatenated raw global buffers and total logical count rather than separate chunks. Only decoded byte count4*N is asserted, so it does not prove value equality or individual chunk correctness. No execution or timing is claimed.

The async test_log/Tokio harness requests RLE across structural encodings with explicit ratio0.8 and BSS disabled. A custom generator repeats i32::MIN, MIN+1 and MIN+2 four times each and requests10000 rows. High-bit values prevent bitpacking savings. The harness is awaited.

The automatic fixture has8000 i32::MIN values followed by a five-value sequence repeated400 times, with BSS disabled. The comment describes a default50% cutoff, while actual shared policy compares costs unless an explicit ratio is supplied. A feature-gated third case encodes2048 runs of four cycling i32::MIN+(run%8), with explicit ratio0.8, BSS disabled and zstd/LZ4 preference. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:174-218)

Private Debug RleDataGenerator stores pattern and cursor. Its unchecked constructor permits an empty pattern. ArrayGenerator::generate ignores requested RowCount and RNG, always emits10000 values cyclically, and advances the cursor; an empty pattern panics. The type is Int32 with element size Some(4).

Block framing tests reject a u64::MAX values-size header and a three-byte payload. The first expects the checked-addition overflow message on64-bit targets; narrower usize conversion could fail earlier with different wording. Tests check error presence/text rather than the variant. Missing payload is not tested locally.
For three i32 ones, the block-header test checks the eight-byte header, values_size4 in little-endian order and total13 bytes. It does not compare all payload bytes or the nested descriptor.
The raw U8 whole-block nine-value test roundtrips and asserts the complete i32 slice via bytemuck. It does not exercise child configuration, empty input or invalid width.

The10000-value block test contains3000 times999,3000 times777 and4000 times555, then asserts exact count and values. Its2048-chunk comments are stale: whole-block RLE only splits runs at the chosen length maximum. The file has38 test functions, including two rstest matrices of four and three cases and one async multi-scenario harness. None ran. Gaps include surplus mini input, zero-count malformed data, custom-child contracts, candidate errors, postcompression chunk budget, width ties and ownership metrics.
